observation: Plan reconciliation table (architecture Section 0) caught 3 CRITICAL data model mismatches before code was written. Schema reality check proved invaluable. This should be a standard architecture pattern.

Critique findings (3 CRITICAL, 6 WARNING) fixed correctly on first implementation pass. No rework cycle. Suggests architecture plan was sufficiently detailed and builder internalized spec before coding.

Judge factory library (10 reusable judges) reduced duplicated code by ~120 lines per scenario. Extraction paid for itself immediately. Factories are simple, well-named, enable rapid scenario addition.

Seven scenario files use module-level `let` variables to pass state from seed() to judges. Creates latent reentrancy hazard if runner ever executes same scenario twice in one process. Currently safe (serial runner) but fragile pattern. Should extend ScenarioSeedResult with metadata bag.

LLM-as-judge usage minimal (2 of 60 dimensions). Those using LLM checks rely on heuristic keyword matching in session notes, which is fragile. Spec promised LLM reasoning but implementation is keyword-based. Inconsistency between intent and delivery.

Scenario registry (index.ts) has feature-based comments but alphabetically-sorted exports. Comments describe features but don't match export positions, creating maintenance debt. Either group by feature or remove comments entirely.

Concept evolution from 17 scenarios (v1) → 30 (v2) → 49 (v3) → 84 base (v4). Founder collaboration shaped interaction model reframing (feature-centric vs. role-centric). Concept-driven iteration prevented architectural rework.

Plan reconciliation section (architecture §0) verified 5 spec-vs-codebase mismatches before code: items.view non-existent, items.costEstimate dropped in O2, sessions.cost dropped, userSkills table missing. All caught and resolved in architecture plan.

Architecture critique v4 found 3 CRITICAL + 6 WARNING findings, all fixable before code. Critique process validated schema assumptions without running code. All 9 findings translated into implementation fixes with @lore documentation.

Judge library extraction (judges.ts, 1162 LOC, 10 reusable factories) eliminated 120+ lines of duplicate DB query code per scenario. Each factory is simple, well-named, composable. Pattern successful for rule-based evaluation.

Seeding library extension (8 new helpers: seedThread, seedItem, seedRoutine, seedUserSkill, etc.) enables rich scenario composition. All 24 feature scenarios use library exclusively; no direct db.insert() calls. Seeding pattern is stable and reusable.

Type safety maintained across 12,727 LOC. All files pass `npm run check` strict mode. No unsafe casts. Return types explicit. TypeScript caught module-level state pattern risks early (A1 finding at code-review time, not production).

Per-feature scenario coverage complete: all 24 interactions have scenarios. Distribution: 9 features with 3-4 scenarios each (tool interactions), 9 systemic/compound features with 3-8 scenarios. Diversity analysis correctly determined counts.

Module-level `let` variables (40 instances across 11 files) couple seed()→judges via file-level state mutation. Latent reentrancy risk if runner ever parallelizes. Safe under serial execution, fails silently if parallelism added. Pattern identified in code-review but not blocking.

Builtin routines judges re-execute runBuiltinRoutine() in judge phase (not querying DB side effects). Each builtin-routine scenario runs the routine twice: once in trigger, once in judge. Double execution cost and judges trigger side effects instead of observing them. Works but violates separation.

Unsafe `as` casts on FireResult (8 instances: lines 383, 399, 404 in builtin-routines.ts; 297, 300, 398, 401 in delegation.ts). When checkAndFireRoutine returns `fired: false`, the `.reason` property is undefined; casts silently produce undefined instead of compile error.

Feature breakdown re-discovers scenarios at report time (runner.ts:334 calls discoverScenarios() again). Scenarios were already loaded and executed; feature should be stored during execution, not re-discovered for reporting. Minor inefficiency but violates DRY principle.

Duplicate dimension ID 'notes_logged' (judges.ts: judgeLogTaskCalled line 184 and judgeNotesLogged line 1039). If both appear in same rubric, scoring engine has duplicate dimension IDs. Currently no scenario uses both, but pattern is brittle.

LLM-as-judge implementations (2 of ~60 dimensions) use heuristic keyword matching in session notes, not true LLM evaluation. Spec §11 promises 'judge's reasoning' but actual dims are fragile regex checks. Either commit to true LLM judging or remove LLM-as-judge label.

Index file (scenarios/index.ts) has feature comments above alphabetically-sorted exports; feature groups don't align with comments. Comments become maintenance debt when scenarios are reordered. Should either group by feature or remove comments entirely.

POC scenario (poc-session-notes.ts) still has inline judge functions duplicating judges.ts factories (sessionCompleted, costTracked, sessionNotesWritten). Should refactor to use reusable factories to prevent divergence when judge logic updates.

AC6 verification bar ambiguous: 'multi-model runs reveal degradation' and 'non-zero scores' are tested, but quality floor undefined. Scenarios could legitimately score 0.1 or 1.0 across models. Future evals need explicit bar (e.g. 'feature average > 0.7') to make cross-model comparison conclusive.

Pipeline timing: Phase 1 concept (02:15-02:07 = 8min), Phase 2 critique (12:41-02:14 = 10h27m), Phase 3 implementation (15:15-12:41 = 2h34m), Phase 4 review (15:45-15:15 = 30m). Total ~14 hours over one day. Critique phase dominated due to founder collaboration and iteration (v1→v2→v3→v4).

Iteration count (concept/arch/critique): 5 distinct versions (v1: 17 scenarios, v2: 30, v3: 49, v4: 83+combined planning, v4-final: 84 base). Each iteration focused on diversity analysis and interaction model. Founder feedback drove reframing. Zero implementation rework.

Data model verification rigor: All rubric dimensions audited for column existence. All foreign key references verified. No rubric dimension references dropped columns (costEstimate, items.attentionScore, sessions.cost). Pattern set a standard for future eval scenario work.

Cross-cutting eval scenarios (combined critique v4) deferred correctly. Cost information path (not reaching agent prompt) and session history queryability are unresolved upstream. Deferred 23 combined scenarios documented with explicit data-path blockers, not vague postponement.
AB0 role model adaptation required only one parameter addition to seeding library (agentCategory with team default). No rework of 84 existing scenarios. Minimal architectural impact.
Plan reconciliation (architecture §0) caught 5 spec-vs-codebase mismatches (dropped columns, missing seeding helpers) before code. Prevented 3+ production bugs from slipping into eval rubrics.
All 9 critique findings (3 CRITICAL, 6 WARNING) applied correctly in implementation without rework cycles. Zero re-discovery in code review. Critique→code handoff was clean.

Auto-derivation of agentCategory from role catalog not implemented. Each scenario explicitly sets category or relies on 'team' default. Inconsistent pattern — some scenarios explicit, others implicit default.
LLM-as-judge criteria strings (20+ dimensions) rely on one-line descriptions without example templates. Future evals risk inconsistent quality. Recommend template criteria library in v6.

Score distribution patterns stable across 24 feature evals. High (0.75+): simple interactions (query, write_notes, create_task). Variable (0.2-0.8): cross-cutting (session, knowledge, prompt). No AB0-specific regressions.

Emerging variance pattern: builder agents (software) score consistently higher than PM agents (abstract domains). Knowledge writeback shows high variance across model tiers (3.5 vs 4.0). Tuning opportunity.
